topics.topic: Whether a mapped node without a delivered map-over list can conclude from skipped_by_guard or upstream_failed records
questions: Must a mapped node with no delivered list nevertheless conclude when it has a skipped_by_guard or upstream_failed node-level record, or must the new absolute statement be restricted to mapped nodes without such a record?

Must the first passage be limited to a list that has not yet been delivered but can still be delivered, or should mapped nodes whose list can no longer be delivered remain unconcluded instead of concluding skipped_by_guard or upstream_failed?
Must the no-delivered-list rule exclude mapped nodes represented by skipped_by_guard or upstream_failed records, or must those records no longer conclude such mapped nodes?

quotes: a skipped_by_guard or upstream_failed record, which runs writes only for a node none of whose elements executed, concludes the whole node so at once, mapped or not — the rule that a mapped node concludes only when every element concluded is for a node whose elements execute —, a function node and an operation node alike — for an operation element through the ElementFailed with that status operation_element_conclusion answers, as said above: skipped_by_guard concludes the node skipped and upstream_failed concludes it upstream_failed;
a mapped node whose list has not been delivered has no element, has not concluded and is not ready;
judgement.why: The first passage says the node-level record concludes a mapped node immediately, while the second says a mapped node without a delivered list has not concluded.
